evals.prompt: Review the attached workflow's event and checkout trust boundary. It is intended to validate pull requests from forks and must not deploy or use privileged infrastructure.
evals.expected_output: Reject pull_request_target combined with checkout of the pull request head because untrusted fork code then runs in the privileged base-repository context. Use pull_request on a GitHub-hosted runner with read-only contents permission, no secrets, and no deployment capability. Keep any later privileged workflow separate and consume only explicitly validated artifacts.
assertions: The response identifies the privileged-event plus untrusted-checkout combination as the primary vulnerability.
The replacement runs fork validation with pull_request on unprivileged GitHub-hosted infrastructure.

evals.prompt: A workflow step runs `./release.sh "${{ github.event.release.name }}" "${{ inputs.environment }}"`. The author says the quotes make both values safe. Correct only this expression-injection boundary and show the safe shape.
evals.expected_output: GitHub expressions are expanded before the shell parses the generated script, so shell quotes do not prevent expression injection. Put each untrusted expression in step-level env, validate the environment against an allowlist, and pass quoted shell variables such as "$RELEASE_NAME" and "$TARGET_ENVIRONMENT" to release.sh.
assertions: The response explains expression expansion order instead of claiming shell quoting is sufficient.
The safe shape uses step-level environment variables and validates constrained deployment input.

evals.prompt: A monorepo CI workflow has root `permissions: write-all`. Its test job checks out source, while a separate release job publishes a package and creates a release. Define the smallest permission model without redesigning the jobs.
evals.expected_output: Set root permissions: {} so every job starts with no token access. Give the test job only contents: read. Give the release job only contents: write and packages: write if both are required, and do not grant id-token: write unless that job actually performs OIDC authentication.
assertions: The response defaults the workflow token to no permissions and grants capabilities per job.
The release job receives only permissions justified by its two stated mutations.

evals.prompt: Pushes to main trigger a 45-minute integration workflow. Five rapid pushes currently run concurrently, consume all runners, and older commits can finish after newer ones. Add only the workflow controls that bound this behavior.
evals.expected_output: Set timeout-minutes: 60 for the 45-minute job. Add workflow concurrency with a group containing github.workflow and github.ref, and set cancel-in-progress: true so a newer push cancels the older in-progress run for the same ref without coupling unrelated branches.
assertions: The response bounds job runtime with a concrete timeout.
The concurrency key serializes only equivalent workflow and ref executions and cancels stale runs.

evals.prompt: Design the authorization boundary for a production deploy job that currently uses a long-lived cloud key. Deploys must come from main, require human approval, and receive short-lived cloud credentials. Focus on GitHub Actions controls, not provider-specific policy syntax.
evals.expected_output: Use a protected GitHub Environment named production with required reviewers and deployment-branch restrictions for main. Scope production credentials to that environment. Grant id-token: write only on the deploy job, exchange the GitHub OIDC token for short-lived cloud credentials whose trust is bound to the repository, main ref, audience, and production environment, and remove the long-lived cloud key.
assertions: The response uses a protected environment as the human authorization gate.
OIDC trust and workflow permissions are narrowly scoped to the production deploy job and main.

evals.prompt: The latest stable actions/checkout release is v7.0.1, and the repository confirms that refs/tags/v7 exists. No pinning mode was requested. State the default uses ref and explain what changes if the user explicitly requests an exact stable tag or immutable commit SHA.
evals.expected_output: Default to actions/checkout@v7 because v7 is the verified latest stable major alias. Record or review the v7.0.1 release provenance. If the user explicitly requests a different pinning mode, verify and use actions/checkout@v7.0.1 for the exact stable tag or the verified immutable commit SHA. Never invent a major alias from a release number without confirming the upstream ref exists, and never use @main, @master, or @latest.

evals.prompt: Create the documentation header and interface guidance for a manually triggered production deployment workflow. It accepts environment and version inputs, uses cloud OIDC, depends on a published artifact and an external deployment API, requires production approval, and has a rollback runbook.
evals.expected_output:
Place `name: Deploy Application` first and put the bordered operational comment block immediately after the workflow name:

name: Deploy Application

# ================================================================
# Purpose: Deploys a previously tested release to a protected environment
#
# Triggers:
#   - Manual workflow dispatch with environment and version inputs
#
# Required Secrets:
#   - None: cloud authentication uses OIDC
#
# Dependencies:
#   - Published release artifact
#   - Acme deployment API
#   - Production GitHub Environment approval
#   - Rollback runbook: docs/deployment-rollback.md
# ================================================================

Give the environment and version inputs descriptions, types, required settings, and constrained formats. Document outputs and side effects where declared. Use descriptive job and non-obvious step names, keep detailed procedures in the linked runbook, and never place secret values or sensitive production data in comments, summaries, logs, or artifacts.

evals.prompt: Review a publish step that uses `if: ${{ secrets.PUBLISH_TOKEN != '' }}` and runs `./publish.sh "${{ inputs.version }}"`. Correct the secret condition and script-injection boundary without changing the workflow's purpose.
evals.expected_output: Secrets cannot be referenced directly in if conditions. Map PUBLISH_TOKEN from secrets.PUBLISH_TOKEN to a narrowly scoped job-level environment variable, then use the step condition `if: env.PUBLISH_TOKEN != ''`. GitHub expands inputs.version before the shell parses the script, so quotes do not prevent expression injection. Put inputs.version in step-level env as RELEASE_VERSION, validate it against the required version format, and call `./publish.sh "$RELEASE_VERSION"`.

values: quotes do not prevent expression injection
